title: Health and Economic Benefits of Chronic Disease Interventions | National Center for Chronic Disease Prevention and Health Promotion (NCCDPHP) | CDC
content: Health and Economic Benefits of Chronic Disease Interventions Apr. 14, 2026 At a glance Chronic diseases are the leading causes of illness, disability, and death in the United States. They are also the leading drivers of our nation's $4.9 trillion in annual health care costs. CDC funds partners to use proven interventions that improve quality of life and save money. Overview Proven chronic disease interventions can be cost-effective. "Cost-effectiveness" recognizes that the cost of the intervention is worthwhile in terms of longer life and better quality of life. Read more about the high cost of chronic conditions and the health and economic benefits of proven interventions in the fact sheets below. Interventions for specific chronic conditions Health and Economic Benefits of Breast Cancer Interventions More screening can reduce late-stage diagnoses and costs. Aug 14, 2025 Health and Economic Benefits of Cervical Cancer Interventions HPV vaccination and routine screening for cervical cancer can reduce cases, deaths, and costs. Aug 15, 2025 Health and Economic Benefits of Colorectal Cancer Interventions Routine screening for colorectal cancer can reduce cases, deaths, and costs. Aug 15, 2025 Health and Economic Benefits of Skin Cancer Interventions Staying safe in the sun and avoiding sunbeds can reduce skin cancer and associated costs. Aug 15, 2025 Health and Economic Benefits of Diabetes Interventions Healthy choices and good diabetes management can reduce cases, complications, and associated costs. July 11, 2024 Health and Economic Benefits of High Blood Pressure Interventions Better management of high blood pressure can lead to less heart disease and fewer strokes. Aug 6, 2025 Health and Economic Benefits of Oral Disease Interventions Dental sealants and community water fluoridation can prevent cavities and save money. Oct 21, 2024 Health and Economic Benefits of Tobacco Use Interventions Avoiding smoking, vaping, and other tobacco use can reduce illness, deaths, and costs.
